name: Alembic vs Supabase migrations discipline
short_definition: Schema change ownership for Python services: one migration runner owns each database (or schema partition). Supabase SQL migrations under `supabase/migrations/` are the source of truth for app Postgres when Supabase/RLS is in play; Alembic owns SQLAlchemy-model-driven private databases. Never dual-migrate the same tables with both tools.
scope_in: Alembic revision/autogenerate/upgrade discipline; Supabase CLI migrations (`db push`, timestamped SQL); single-writer ownership rules; expand-contract zero-downtime; RLS-in-migration gates; deploy ordering (migrate then code); forward-fix vs downgrade in prod; branching/merge conflicts; seed vs migrate separation.
scope_out: ORM query patterns (py-sqlalchemy-async / py-sql-first-boundaries); pool sizing (py-db-pool-lifecycle); app business logic; data warehouse ETL; NoSQL migrations; client-only localStorage schema.
defaults: Pick ONE owner per Postgres target. Monorepo with Supabase (engineer default): all public schema + RLS + functions live in `supabase/migrations/{timestamp}_{verb}_{subject}.sql`; Python services consume the schema via async SQLAlchemy/asyncpg or supabase-py — they do NOT run Alembic against that DB. Pure Python service with private Postgres (no Supabase CLI): Alembic + SQLAlchemy 2 metadata, autogenerate as draft only, human-reviewed revisions, `alembic upgrade head` in migrate job before app deploy. Expand-contract for breaking column renames. Prefer forward-fix migrations in production over `downgrade`. Never edit applied migration files; add a new revision. CI: migration apply on main, RLS check on every CREATE TABLE in public, type regen after schema change.
decision_gates: USE Supabase migrations when: shared app DB with RLS, Auth, Realtime, Edge; monorepo Next+Python sharing tables; team already uses `supabase db push`. USE Alembic when: Python-owned private DB, multi-schema SQLAlchemy models as primary DDL source, no Supabase migration history. USE Atlas/migra only as audit/diff helpers — not second writers without policy. DO NOT run Alembic autogenerate against Supabase-managed public tables while also applying supabase SQL — history diverges. DO NOT apply prod migrations from laptops without backup/approval. Split data backfills from schema DDL when locks risk downtime.
do_dont: DO: one linear (or explicitly merged) history; review every autogenerated Alembic op; enable RLS in same migration as CREATE TABLE public.*; index FKs and policy columns; expand then deploy code then contract; test migrations on empty + realistic data; pin Alembic with SQLAlchemy in lockfile. DON'T: dashboard SQL on remote once migrations own the DB; dual Alembic+Supabase on same tables; trust autogenerate blindly (server defaults, CHECK, RLS, indexes, enums often wrong); long exclusive locks on hot tables without plan; deploy code that needs columns before migrate; commit secrets in SQL seeds.
code_skeleton:
# --- Supabase-owned (default monorepo) ---
# supabase/migrations/20260713120000_create_jobs.sql
# create table public.jobs (
#   id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
#   user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
#   status text not null default 'pending',
#   created_at timestamptz not null default now()
# );
# create index jobs_user_id_idx on public.jobs (user_id);
# alter table public.jobs enable row level security;
# create policy "Users read own jobs" on public.jobs for select
#   to authenticated using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);

# CI / local
# supabase db push
# supabase gen types typescript --linked > packages/types/database.ts

# --- Alembic-owned private DB ---
# pyproject: alembic>=1.18,<2 sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0
# alembic.ini + alembic/env.py target_metadata = Base.metadata
# alembic revision --autogenerate -m "add jobs"
# # REVIEW then:
# alembic upgrade head

# env.py sketch (async)
# from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import async_engine_from_config
# def run_migrations_online():
#     connectable = async_engine_from_config(...)
#     async with connectable.connect() as conn:
#         await conn.run_sync(do_run_migrations)

# Expand-contract rename:
# 1) add new_col nullable
# 2) deploy dual-write/read code
# 3) backfill
# 4) make new_col NOT NULL, drop old_col
failure_modes: 1) Dual migration tools fight over same tables → drift and failed push. 2) Dashboard edits desync migration history. 3) Autogenerate drops columns/indexes incorrectly. 4) Code deploy before migrate → runtime MissingColumn. 5) Long ALTER TABLE locks production. 6) Missing RLS on new public tables. 7) Irreversible data loss from naive downgrade. 8) Branch merge produces two heads without merge revision. 9) Seeds mixed into migrations break re-runs. 10) Running Alembic and Supabase against same alembic_version / schema_migrations without coordination.
anti_patterns: CREATE TABLE in app startup metadata.create_all for production; editing old migration files after apply; storing only ORM models without SQL migrations when Supabase owns RLS; skipping review of autogenerate; `downgrade` as primary prod rollback; one mega-migration per quarter; migrations that require interactive prompts; putting service_role keys in seed files; dual-writing schema from TS drizzle and Python Alembic on same DB without explicit partition.
tools: Primary (Supabase path): Supabase CLI, timestamped SQL in supabase/migrations, check-rls-migration.sh, pgTAP. Primary (Python private DB): Alembic + SQLAlchemy 2. Audit/diff optional: Atlas, migra — not second writers. CI: supabase db push / alembic upgrade head as migrate job. Alternatives: Django migrations (Django-only), Flyway/Liquibase (polyglot ops) — not default for this stack.
versions_as_of: as_of 2026-07-13: Alembic 1.18.x (PyPI 1.18.5 series Jun 2026); SQLAlchemy 2.0.x required for modern Alembic; Supabase CLI migration workflow per official docs (timestamp SQL, db push, no remote dashboard schema edits once migrations own DB). Pin alembic and sqlalchemy in uv.lock.
config_snippets:
# pyproject.toml (Alembic-owned service)
[project]
dependencies = [
  "sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.36",
  "asyncpg>=0.30",
  "alembic>=1.18,<2",
]

# Makefile / CI migrate step (Alembic)
# uv run alembic upgrade head
# uv run alembic check   # optional drift check vs models

# Supabase CI (owned path)
# supabase db push --linked
# bash scripts/check-rls-migration.sh supabase/migrations/*.sql

# Deploy order
# 1) migrate job succeeds
# 2) deploy API/workers
# 3) regenerate TS/Python types if needed
deprecation_watch: metadata.create_all as production migrator; South (Django ancient); raw unversioned SQL dumps as the only history; concurrent Alembic+Supabase writers; editing live prod schema in Studio without migration file; relying on alembic downgrade in prod as SOP.
ts_boundary: Next/TS types come from Supabase generated `database.ts` (or OpenAPI from FastAPI for non-DB contracts). When Supabase owns schema, Python models must track migrations — regenerate or hand-sync SQLAlchemy models after SQL lands. Never invent columns only in Python without a migration PR. Expand-contract coordinates TS + Python deploys.
rust_boundary: Rust/sqlx or Diesel migrations: same single-owner rule — if Supabase owns public schema, Rust uses query-only against migrated DB. Private Rust service DB may use its own sqlx migrate. Do not have Python Alembic and sqlx both mutate the same schema.
supabase_boundary: Golden rule: never change remote schema outside migrations once migration history is established. RLS policies, grants, and functions belong in SQL migrations. Python service_role bypasses RLS — still requires correct schema from migrations. Auth hooks/triggers: SQL migrations, not ad-hoc Studio.
boundary_contracts: Migration files are the contract for schema. Env: DATABASE_URL / SUPABASE_DB_URL for migrate jobs only (not app runtime if using pooler incorrectly). OpenAPI does not replace migrations. MCP tools must not apply DDL in prod. Document which service owns which schema in monorepo README.
decision_matrix_row: Problem: shared app schema + RLS with Next → Supabase SQL migrations. Problem: Python-only private Postgres + SQLAlchemy models → Alembic. Problem: zero-downtime rename → expand-contract multi-PR. Problem: polyglot high-control DDL ops → consider Atlas as linter/diff, keep one apply path.
threats: Destructive migrations wiping data; privilege escalation via GRANT in unchecked SQL; RLS disabled on new tables exposing rows via anon/authenticated; SQL injection in dynamic migration scripts; secrets in seed SQL committed to git; migration runner with superuser broader than needed.
mitigations: PR review for all migrations; RLS gate script; least-privilege migrator role where possible; backup before prod migrate; no user input in migration generation; secrets only via CI vault; staging apply before prod; ban Dashboard DDL on managed envs.
agent_codegen_policy: MUST: choose single migration owner; put RLS with CREATE TABLE public; review autogenerate; forward-fix for prod mistakes; migrate-before-code deploy order. MUST NOT: create_all in prod; dual Alembic+Supabase on same tables; edit applied revisions; skip RLS; generate destructive DROP without explicit human intent in PR description.
tests_required: Apply full migration chain on empty DB in CI; optional second pass with seed; RLS pgTAP for new tables; Alembic `upgrade head` + `downgrade` smoke on disposable DB for private services; expand-contract dual-write tests when renaming hot columns.
ci_gates: Migration apply job; check-rls-migration on supabase path; alembic upgrade on private DB path; fail if models drift (optional alembic check); no service_role keys in SQL; types regen check for TS.
skill_scan_signals: POSITIVE: supabase/migrations timestamp files; alembic/versions reviewed ops; enable row level security with CREATE TABLE; expand-contract comments; migrate job before deploy. NEGATIVE: metadata.create_all in lifespan for prod; both alembic and supabase mutating same tables; Dashboard-only schema; missing RLS; autogenerate committed without review comments; secrets in .sql seeds.
skill_module_bullets:
- One migration owner per database: Supabase SQL OR Alembic — never both on same tables.
- Supabase monorepo default: `supabase/migrations/` + RLS gates; Python consumes schema.
- Alembic: autogenerate is draft; human review required; pin with SQLAlchemy 2.
- Deploy: migrate → code; expand-contract for breaking changes.
- Prod: forward-fix > downgrade; no laptop-only prod DDL.
- Never edit applied migration files; add new revisions.
action_items: 1) Document ownership matrix in references/python.md. 2) Scan for create_all and dual migrators. 3) Wire RLS gate + migrate-before-deploy in CI template. 4) Cross-link deploy-ops and backend-database. 5) Example Alembic async env.py in skill snippets.

conflicts_noted: Some Python tutorials default Alembic for everything including Supabase — conflicts with monorepo Supabase-as-truth and RLS workflow. Atlas marketing pushes replace Alembic; still treat as optional tooling unless team standardizes. Downgrade in prod advocated by some guides — ops practice prefers forward-fix. Community split on squashing long histories — squash only with coordinated baseline procedure.
